extracted.intended_audience: Readers of The New Yorker who want to enter or vote in the Cartoon Caption Contest (age 13+).
extracted.subtask_description: Submit humorous captions to The New Yorker’s weekly Cartoon Caption Contest: each week a cartoon is posted, readers submit captions, the editors pick three finalists, and readers vote for a winner; entrants/voters must be at least 13 years old. Finalists and winners are published online and in the magazine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weekly submission process
rubrics_metrics.description: "Each week, we provide a cartoon in need of a caption. You, the reader, submit your caption below, we choose three finalists, and you vote for your favorite.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process is weekly: submit a caption for the posted cartoon; editors choose three finalists from submissions; readers later vote among the finalists for the winner. Finalists for a given cartoon will appear online on a specified date and in a future issue of the magazine (example: "Finalists for this week’s cartoon, by Mort Gerberg, will appear online January 14th and in the January 20th, 2020, issue of The New Yorker").

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — age requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: "Anyone age thirteen or older can enter or vote.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants and voters must be at least 13 years old. (The page references complete rules for further eligibility details.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Finalist selection and publication
rubrics_metrics.description: "we choose three finalists... Finalists for this week’s cartoon... will appear online [date] and in the [issue date] issue of The New Yorker.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors select three finalist captions from reader submissions; those finalists are published online and printed in a future magazine issue. Example dates are provided on the page for when finalists and winners will be posted/published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader participation in preliminary rating
rubrics_metrics.description: "Help us pick three finalists from last week’s contest by rating submissions.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers may be asked to rate or evaluate submissions to help narrow entries to the three finalists (link/button shown as "Vote now" or similar). This indicates a reader-driven rating step exists in the selection pipeline in addition to editor selection of finalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting for the winner
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the three finalists are posted, readers vote to choose the winner among those finalists. The site provides an interface for voting on finalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of winners and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Example winner announcements (format): caption, author name, city, placement (winner/second/third).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winners and runners-up are publicly announced with the caption text, contributor name, location, and placement (e.g., winner, second place, third place); past examples appear on the page. This implies criteria of selection result in ranked placements published by the magazine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site terms and acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: "Use of and/or registration on any portion of this site constitutes acceptance of our User Agreement (updated 1/1/20) and Privacy Policy and Cookie Statement (updated 1/1/20).","
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting or registering to participate implies acceptance of the site’s User Agreement and Privacy Policy. Entrants should consult the complete rules (linked) for full terms and any additional contest rules or restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to complete contest rules
rubrics_metrics.description: "To read the complete rules, click here.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explicitly refers entrants to a separate complete rules document (not reproduced on this page) for full terms, detailed eligibility, submission restrictions, intellectual-property/usage rules, deadlines, and other requirements — entrants should review that linked document for comprehensive rules beyond the overview on this page.
